problem_markdown: A set $S$ of $n$ plane points has no three collinear. From every point, at least $k$ other points are at one common distance. Prove $k<1/2+\sqrt{2n}$.
solutions_markdown:
Count pairs $(P,\{A,B\})$ of distinct points of $S$ with $PA=PB$. For each apex $P$, the hypothesis supplies at least $\binom k2$ such unordered bases, so the count is at least $n\binom k2$.

For each base $\{A,B\}$, possible apexes lie on its perpendicular bisector. At most two points of $S$ lie on that line, since no three are collinear. Thus the count is at most $2\binom n2=n(n-1)$.

Consequently $k(k-1)\le2(n-1)$, or $(k-1/2)^2\le2n-7/4<2n$. Since $k\ge1$, taking square roots proves $k<1/2+\sqrt{2n}$.
